questions.subtopic: Case Analysis: Demand Deposit Cheque Clearance
questions.question: A furniture maker sells desks to a school and receives a crossed account-payee cheque of ₹1,20,000. Why is this payment method safer for both parties than carrying ₹1,20,000 in paper currency notes?
options: It allows the school to cancel payment after three years without reason
It exempts the furniture maker from paying sales tax
It eliminates the risk of physical cash theft, provides an indisputable bank transaction record, and transfers funds directly between verified accounts
It guarantees that the bank will pay double the cheque amount
questions.explanation: Cheques provide secure, paperless audit trails, eliminate cash handling risks, and ensure safe interbank transfer directly between authorized payees.

questions.subtopic: RBI Policy Mandate on Priority Lending
questions.question: Why does NCERT say the RBI supervises banks to check that credit reaches small borrowers as well as profit-making businesses?
options: To ensure that lending is not limited to profit-making businesses and traders and also reaches small cultivators, small-scale industries and small borrowers
Banks would distribute free cash grants to all citizens
All urban industrial companies would go bankrupt
The national poverty rate would drop to zero overnight
questions.explanation: NCERT describes RBI supervision as a way to monitor formal lending and ensure that banks also lend to small cultivators, small-scale industries and small borrowers. The original counterfactual that credit would flow exclusively to large conglomerates was too absolute and not established by the chapter.

Cooperatives are owned exclusively by foreign sovereign states
Private commercial banks are legally forbidden to accept deposits
Cooperatives do not charge any interest on loans
questions.explanation: Cooperatives are member-owned mutual aid institutions that operate on democratic 'one member, one vote' principles to provide low-cost credit to farmers.

questions.subtopic: Poverty Alleviation and Formal Credit Expansion
questions.question: Why is expanding access to affordable formal credit in rural areas important for development?
options: It can reduce dependence on higher-cost informal credit and help households and producers access loans on more reasonable terms
It gives free tractors to every villager who opens a bank account
It eliminates the need for agricultural crop cultivation
It guarantees that every rural borrower will become debt-free
questions.explanation: NCERT argues that banks and cooperatives should lend more, particularly in rural areas, so dependence on expensive informal credit can reduce. More equal access to formal credit can help poorer households and small producers borrow at more reasonable rates and support economic activity. This is a development measure, not an automatic guarantee of poverty elimination.

questions.subtopic: Summary: Financial Inclusion Vision
questions.question: Which comprehensive policy encapsulates India's national goal for the 'Money and Credit' sector?
options: Abolishing all paper money and returning to a 100% barter exchange economy
Allowing private moneylenders to set interest rates without any government oversight
Prohibiting rural women from opening individual bank savings accounts
Universal financial inclusion through accessible formal banking, widespread SHG micro-credit networks, transparent collateral terms, and equitable credit flow to small producers
questions.explanation: National economic development requires universal financial inclusion: expanding affordable formal credit to all citizens, particularly small farmers, artisans, and women's SHGs.
